value.hook: Before splitting shutdown phases into tasks or citing per-phase duration and cancellation safety
value.title: Shutdown task ownership and timer origin are separate proofs

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Open when shutdown work is moved into spawned tasks or phase durations are cited.

F267 step2 passed29 controls and killed four mutants: phase task separation,
printable naming, clear-on-SpawnHold-Drop and stop-first selection. SpawnHold
clears metadata before releasing the owned mutex on return and unwind; revive
uses the same hold through prechecks and launch.

Distinguish three guarantees. A normally returned shutdown joins all twelve
phase tasks before flush/store close. Dropping the join future detaches its
already-spawned task; a latch proved work finished after cancellation. A release
started before the join can finish after an empty HTTP drain; that order was
also unconstrained before this change. The real private-tmux/open-stream ordering
test passed at the reviewed head.

Timers on already-running HTTP/release work are remaining join waits, not full
signal-to-completion times. Separate tasks fix shared-task starvation but do not
change where those timers begin. Main's CLI awaits shutdown without cancelling.

Magic wand: keep normal return, panic, cancellation and timer-origin witnesses
as separate shutdown proof rows instead of generalizing one green timing test.
